title: Molly Ringwald Says ‘Secret Life of the American Teenager’ Was Her ‘Worst’ Work Experience: ‘One Person Was Really Difficult’
description:
Molly Ringwald’s experience starring in “The Secret Life of the American Teenager” was tarnished by one bad apple on set.

	The veteran actress was
body:
Molly Ringwald’s experience starring in “The Secret Life of the American Teenager” was tarnished by one bad apple on set.

	The veteran actress was a guest on the Aug. 4 episode of Andy Cohen’s Bravo talk show “Watch What Happens Live,” which is known for posing revealing questions during games with celebrity guests.

	During a round of “Spill the IMDB Tea,” Cohen asked Ringwald to rank some of her past work on a scale of 1 to 10 based on her experience. She put the drama series, which starred Shailene Woodley as a pregnant teenager who is the daughter of Ringwald’s character, at the bottom of the ranking.
	

	“The worst is ‘one’? OK, that was it. The worst,” Ringwald says. “It was a hard, I mean … OK, I love the cast. I love Shailene [Woodley]. There was one person that was really difficult. And I’m not gonna say who that one person is, [but] they brought it down to a one.”


	“Secret Life” ran from 2008-2013, and Ringwald was a series regular for the first four seasons and a special guest star during the show’s fifth and final season. Ken Baumann, Mark Derwin, India Eisley, Greg Finley and Steve Schirripa also starred on the show.

	Elsewhere in the game, Ringwald cited “Pretty in Pink” as her favorite project.

	“That was pretty great … I’ll give that a 10,” Ringwald says. “It was written for me. [John Hughes] wrote the movie for me and, you know, I actually have a collage that I made myself that’s in the bedroom.”

	She was also asked about “Diff’rent Strokes,” “The Facts of Life,” “Not Another Teen Movie,” “Teaching Mrs. Tingle” and “Jem and the Holograms.”
	

	Watch the “Watch What Happens Live” clip below.

schema.headline: Molly Ringwald Says ‘Secret Life of the American Teenager’ Was Her ‘Worst’ Work Experience: ‘One Person Was Really Difficult’

title: Xbox Celebrates 25 Years With New Community Designs, Updates and FanFest Tour Dates (Gaming News Roundup)
description: Xbox is celebrating 25 years of play with new updates, community designs, curated Game Pass collections and the FanFest Tour schedule. Xbox’s 25th a
body:
Xbox is celebrating 25 years of play with new updates, community designs, curated Game Pass collections and the FanFest Tour schedule. Xbox’s 25th anniversary is Nov. 15.

	In partnership with community creators Klobrille and Ben Kenobi, Xbox is publishing a collection of gamerpics, backgrounds and a dynamic console theme. The collection is available today.

	Beginning today, players who sign into their Xbox account on console, PC or the mobile app will receive the Xbox 25th Anniversary profile badge, available through the end of 2026.
	

	Curated Game Pass collections bring together games from franchises that defined each Xbox generation, available on console and PC. Included are titles like “Fable Anniversary,” “Halo: The Master Chief Collection,” “Fallout 4” and “Psychonauts 2.”


	Xbox FanFest Tour 2026 kicked off at the Xbox Games Showcase in Los Angeles June 7.  The tour continues Aug. 26 at gamescom in Cologne, Germany,  Sept. 17 during Tokyo Game Show in Tokyo, Sept. 26 in London, Oct. 17 in Mexico City, Mexico, Oct. 17 in Sydney, Australia and Nov. 6 in Toronto, Canada. More information is coming soon for a date in Seattle.

	See more gaming news from this week in the roundup below.
	
		PARTNERSHIPS/COLLABS	

	Addison Rae is joining the Fortnite Icon Series starting Aug. 6. 

	Coming to the online gaming platform is the Addison Rae Outfit, which features her all-pink outfit from her “Fame is a Gun” music video, complete with a sunglass toggle. Also arriving is the Famous Addison Rae Outfit inspired by her on-stage looks, available in white, Fame Brite (pink and yellow) and Soda Black. 
	

	The musician-turned-influencer is also introducing two new Jam Tracks and emotes for her singles “Diet Pepsi” and “fame is a Gun.” The Turtle-on-Moon Back Bling and Addison’s Sundae Back Bling can also be purchased, along with the Fame Scepter Pickaxe and the reactive Addison’s Biggest Fan Pickaxe. 
	
		IN-GAME EVENTS	

	KRAFTON, Inc. and CurseForge announced the PUBG: Battlegrounds UGC Contest, a global creator competition with a $95,000 prize in celebration of the upcoming launch of PUBG: Playgrounds. The contest will launch Aug. 12.

	Players and modders can submit original experiences in three categories: combat, survival and creative. Thirty winning modes are planned to be released through PUBG: Playgrounds, giving creators a platform to share their work.

	Each category features a $25,000 prize pool, including a $10,000 first-place award and prizes for the top 10 entries. Ten additional creators will receive $500 mid-contest prizes, and six community favorites selected through public voting will receive $2,500 each.

	Submissions are open Aug. 12 through Sept. 2. Community voting is open Sept. 6-9. Winners will be announced Sept. 14.

	PUBG: Playgrounds is an upcoming game hub within PUBG: Battlegrounds where players can discover and play community-created experiences. The hub will be accessible through the PUBG Play menu and gives player-created mods an in-game home.
	
		TABLETOP/RPG GAMES	

	Wizards of the Coast announced Secret Lair Commander Deck: Hatsune Miku, a ready-to-play 100-card Commander deck. 

	The virtual singer joins the Commander table for the first Universes Beyond Secret Lair Commander Deck, which will be headlined by Trostani, Selesnya’s Voice as “Miku, Song of the People.” It will include one Commander deck, ten double-sided tokens, one Trostani and one deck box.

	Thirteen cards with new art will also be featured in the deck. There will be a 24-hour window to order Secret Lair Commander Deck: Hatsune Miku starting Monday at 9 a.m. PT and ending Tuesday at the same time.

	“Built around a classic green-white lifegain strategy, Secret Lair Commander Deck: Hatsune Miku plays exactly like a great Miku performance feels: joyful, communal and bigger with every verse,” the Commander deck’s description reads. “Cards like Archangel of Thune, Aetherflux Reservoir, Crested Sunmare, Rhys the Redeemed, Voice of the Blessed, and Mirari’s Wake help players build an ever-growing board state, gain life in huge bursts and transform that life total into a win condition.”

title: Sienna Spiro on Writing Candidly as a Young Woman, While Being Frank About Adoring Sinatra and Twiggy: ‘Being 20 Is Just Tricky, Period’
description: Sienna Spiro was something of an established artist even before her debut full-length album, “Visitor,” came out on July 3. The 20-year-old Londoner
body:
Sienna Spiro was something of an established artist even before her debut full-length album, “Visitor,” came out on July 3. The 20-year-old Londoner with the big ’60s hair and an even bigger, more timeless voice is officially a freshman — she will almost certainly be up for a best new artist Grammy in a few months — but she’s also already a role model. 

	Not that this has occurred to her yet. “Really?” she says when I point out this dichotomy over a Zoom call shortly after the record’s release, a little bit surprised that anyone could consider her an influential or entrenched figure in pop music just yet. 
	

	So here’s the case for her already being a star, and a true influencer: The new LP was preceded by a series of star-making singles, like the glorious ballad “Die on This Hill,” which went Top 20 in America and Top 10 in her native U.K. That led to a series of media-galvanizing shows, like a U.S. headlining debut in L.A. at the Troubadour in March that had me raving about her in Variety as “the world’s next great pop vocal superhero.” A tour of bigger North American theaters set for this October sold out immediately, with her album not yet released, as skyrocketing resale prices suggested that the amphitheater circuit would have been within reach for her.


	But perhaps the most telling sign of her impact is how many of the young women participating in competitive TV singing shows have decided that covering her original songs is the best way to make an impression in an audition. On a spring episode of “American Idol,” for instance, a standout candidate tried out by covering Spiro’s “Maybe.” That was followed by Luke Bryan saying the judges had already heard  other “Idol” contestants try out with Spiro’s song — and maybe were already weary of it — but at last they’d found an aspirant who could nail it.
	

	Spiro brightens on the rainy stoop where she’s sitting, delighted to hear that in the world of “Idol,” her nascent singles are already considered standards. “Whenever I hear of someone doing that,” she says, “it’s so crazy to me because when I was younger, me and my little sister would do ‘Britain’s Got Talent’ in my mom’s bedroom, pretending to audition.” She has been able to pass go and skip having a reality-show step in her career, but she’s tickled to be covered by even more youthful singers who’ve come to consider her the gold standard. Spiro may only be 20, but she’s probably just a step or two away from acolytes calling her “Mother.”

	Speaking of finding hills to die on, I’m ready to collapse on a mound proclaiming that Spiro’s is a voice for the ages, or at least one that I expect to be hearing for decades to come. It doesn’t hurt that she’s inculcated in the classics and is unafraid to follow in some very big footsteps. She’s most often compared to Adele, who laid the groundwork for husky belts like hers to succeed. But conversation about her favorite albums is bound to lead to Spiro sharing her adoration for Frank Sinatra’s lonesome 1955 classic “In the Wee Small Hours.” “You know, one of the reasons I signed to Capitol was because I wanted their logo on my vinyl to match Frank’s,” she confesses. 

	Chalk it up in part to a dad who grew up in the ’60s and implanted that era in her soul, although only fairly recently has she added a visual complement to her throwback musical loves by adopting a bouffant and a minidress, styling herself like she was straight out of Swinging London, if not singlehandedly reviving the Ronettes.

	When Spiro recently did a how-to video for Vogue before a concert (yes, she does her own makeup), she cited Twiggy as an influence as she went through the steps to putting her cat-eye liner in place. “You’re drawn to what you’re drawn to, but I love the ’60s,” she says. “I just loved all her magazine covers, and the way her eyes look was so fascinating to me. When I was figuring out my identity growing up, I loved her, so I wanted to try it.” 

	If you’ve seen the video Spiro put up as a blond lass just starting out at 16, sending her cover of a Finneas number into the world like a message in a bottle, she’s unrecognizable. “I grew up really insecure, and much bigger in weight to all of my peers and family, so I’ve always had issues with the way I dress. But my dad always showed me the music and the films of women like Barbra Streisand and Ava Gardner. When I started releasing music, I still didn’t want anyone to see my body, so I would wear huge clothes so that no one would get to make any comments. Then you grow into yourself more. I tried the hair for the first time, and it made me feel like such an elevated version of myself.”
	

	Her songs match the promise of her voice, but there’s very little that’s retro about them, at least lyrically; they’re mostly too stripped down and confessional to suggest any era but that of a contemporary young woman who’s writing very frankly. “I have no filter, which is a good thing and a bad thing. But I have no choice but to write honestly, and no choice other than to show up as myself,” she says. “I’m just a 20-year-old, and sometimes I wake up and I’m on my period and I have to go and perform onstage. And sometimes having hair that’s different from my everyday hair, or when I put my boots on, allows me to kind of step into something and have a level of confidence and separation from the way I felt writing those songs.” But she certainly doesn’t step into them every day: Without the big hair, she goes unrecognized on the stoop for the length of our video call. And, she points out, “I’d never wear heels in everyday life.”

	Famously, at this point, she has vocal nodules that are responsible for the quality of her voice. “I was really husky growing up,” Spiro says. “I only officially found out [about the nodules] two years ago. But I’ve always had a super raspy voice. I do feel like I’ve probably always had them, or from a young age at least.” Half the world’s young female singers would probably pay hundreds of thousands of dollars for those nodules, I note, and she laughs. “You definitely wouldn’t. A nightmare! They’re such a blessing and a curse. I love the texture they give my voice, and sometimes they stop your voice from doing something, which I actually think sounds good. But I was nearly mute for a year — like, I barely spoke the year before last. It was really tricky. Very isolating.” And ultimately very empowering, when she came back out of it in full strength, sounding 20-going-on-40, a one-woman tonic for anyone who’s had their share of wispy voices in pop.

	She credits her primary producer, Omer Fedi, for helping teach her the vocal quality she cherishes most: “Intentionality.” Before Fedi put her back on the right track in the early making of “Visitor,” she went through a phase of trying too hard in the studio before comprehending that, while we love artists who overshare, we don’t necessarily love the ones who over-sing. 
	

	“I didn’t grow up thinking I was a singer, ever. My dad always was like, ‘Oh, you sound shit,’ and I was like, ‘OK, great — so I’ve got to be a really good songwriter if I wanna do this as a job.’ But then I started doing sessions, and people started being very complimentary of my voice, so then I fed off that validation, and so I would do the most. Every riff, every run, every moment to belt, I would take it. But the way Sinatra sings is like a painter.”

	The lead vocal she most aspires to live up to, though, is Roberta Flack’s 1971 cover of “Will You Love Me Tomorrow.” “The way she approaches each line is with so much care. When I listen to it, I just feel like melting. You’d think a favorite vocal performance would be something like Whitney Houston, which obviously is up there for me. But that is a dream of mine, to be able to sing like [Flack]. Sometimes holding back and being quiet is the most powerful thing you can do.” As far as most fans are concerned, Spiro’s already mastered the art of creating meltdowns: Every time she sings, there are happy puddles where listeners once stood.   

	“Visitor” isn’t quite a concept album, but the title stems from her coming back around again and again to the theme of “impermanence,” and how disturbing that can be until you find a way to embrace it. It’s not unusual, among her peer group, to focus on relationships inevitably ending, but Spiro goes on from that to address the way all things — and mortality itself — must pass, which can be a little heady to be hearing from a 20-year-old.

	“Sorry, it’s raining now,” she notes, explaining why she might be feeling “super existential,” though it’s clearly her natural way of being. “I’m neurodivergent, and I think that’s a really big part of the hyper-fixating and overanalyzing. If I feel something, I will sit there for hours, days, weeks and years trying to understand why it is I feel that way. It took nine tries for me to write [the song] ‘The Visitor,’ because it was years of ‘Why do I feel like this? What causes it?’ 

	“My grandma feels these feelings, and you can feel it when you’re 10 years old in a playground, feeling like you’re not getting chosen. You feel it when you’re in your early 20s and going through your first heartbreak, or seeing how your old friends aren’t really your friends anymore. Or finding your identity while knowing how fragile your existence is. My grandpa died, and you have people leave your life in that way. We are all visitors in life in some way, shape or form. And this whole album is me grappling with coming to terms with that.”
	

	Somehow out of these feelings about life being transitory, Spiro finds a momentary fix in focusing on physical media. For example, the song she recorded for the “Devil Wears Prada 2” soundtrack, “Material Lover,” specifically came out of reflecting on the film’s storyline and how it addresses the threat of print publications going away. “I really related to the idea of magazines ceasing getting printed as everything becomes digital with social media. I’m 20 years old, and that’s very much apparent in my generation, and I hate it. I especially hate how it translates across to music. I really believe in having tangible, real, physical things everywhere in life, but music is the thing I’m the closest to.”  She did a photo shoot picturing herself amid the colored vinyl variants for the new album. “I love these old hi-fi and analog adverts, and I set up that whole shoot inspired by it. Holding your music in physical form is just a really crazy feeling. Music comes out of nowhere — it comes out of your head — and you’re like, ‘I don’t even know how this even came to be.’ But then when you get to hold it in a physical format, it makes it feel real.”

	Spiro will be the guest performer at Variety‘s annual Power of Young Hollywood event, where she will join a lineup of honorees who are mostly also in their early 20s to sing “Pure,” a bubbling-under track from the new album. She will undoubtedly be able to compare notes with some of her contemporaries at that event. Spiro acknowledges it can be difficult navigating life as an old soul who not so long ago was being made to feel like a child prodigy; after teenaged years of being told she was great for her age, now she has to go for just being great. Which, as “Visitor” proves, is hardly a formidable task. But finding the sweet spot where she can embrace her youth while looking toward a kind of agelessness can be a challenge.

	“Being 20 is just tricky, period,” she laughs. “Everyone struggles. But in the industry, for some reason, it’s really been great to be super young. But you’re put in these really trying situations where you have to be mature and make decisions about your life and do sessions with people that are twice your age. And so it’s a really weird balance of ‘Oh, I’m super young’ yet needing to be mature to make good decisions… while also making sure I’m still being youthful and having life experience so I can continue to write songs and grow as a human… while also making sure I’m not damaging anything for my life being in these situations. There’s a balance you have to figure out — which I’ve definitely not figured out! So that’s my experience with my age.”
	

	Dichotomies suit Spiro. File her under “New Arrivals,” but know that, by any intuitive standard, she’s already a fixture.

schema.headline: Sienna Spiro on Writing Candidly as a Young Woman, While Being Frank About Adoring Sinatra and Twiggy: ‘Being 20 Is Just Tricky, Period’

title: Carson Daly Not Quitting ‘The Voice’ and Says Keke Palmer Is Hosting ‘Celebrity’ Spinoff in 2027 Because She’s ‘Perfect For It’
description: Carson Daly has commented on why Keke Palmer is hosting “The Voice: Celebrity,” an upcoming spinoff of the NBC singing competition he’s hosted for 1
body:
Carson Daly has commented on why Keke Palmer is hosting “The Voice: Celebrity,” an upcoming spinoff of the NBC singing competition he’s hosted for 15 years.

	After praising the new series as a “fun, new idea” that he’s “been talking about on ‘The Today Show’ for a while now,” he wrote in an Instagram caption that he is “not the right host for it. We have a NEW amazing HOST! The triple threat queen @keke who is PERFECT for it! I’m so grateful she carved out the time in her busy career to help us out. We’re all big fans & welcome her to the family.”
	

	Clarifying further, he added, “Many today have asked if I’m leaving the show. Nope. We’re gonna try out these 2 formats this fall/spring & see how it goes! Hopefully this post clears up any confusion. I am still hosting the show currently. In fact, I have hosted & produced every single second of the show since day 1.” He also noted that he’ll serve as a producer on “The Voice: Celebrity” and “helping it launch from behind the scenes.”


	Palmer’s casting as the host of “The Voice: Celebrity” was reported on Tuesday; she joins the series alongside Joe Jonas, Queen Latifah and Riley Green, who will serve as coaches. Jonas will be a first-time “Voice” coach, whereas Latifah and Green will be returners to the franchise after making their debuts on “The Voice” Season 31 this fall. “The Voice: Celebrity” will premiere in 2027.

	“The Voice” is produced by MGM Alternative, Warner Horizon Unscripted Television and ITV Studios ’ The Voice USA, Inc. John de Mol created the series and serves as executive producer alongside Mark Burnett, Audrey Morrissey, Amanda Zucker, Kyra Thompson, Adam H. Sher and Barry Poznick.

schema.headline: Carson Daly Not Quitting ‘The Voice’ and Says Keke Palmer Is Hosting ‘Celebrity’ Spinoff in 2027 Because She’s ‘Perfect For It’

title: ‘I Love LA’ Season 2: Taron Egerton, Jamie Chung Among 6 Cast in Guest Star Roles
description:
“I Love LA” has added six new guest stars to its upcoming second season, Variety has learned. 

	The HBO comedy series has cast Taron Egerton (“Apex
body:
“I Love LA” has added six new guest stars to its upcoming second season, Variety has learned. 

	The HBO comedy series has cast Taron Egerton (“Apex,” “Rocketman”), Jamie Chung (“Lovecraft Country,” “Batman: Caped Crusader”), Bejamin Norris (“Never Have I Ever,” “Abbott Elementary”), Dylan Arnold (“Oppenheimer,’ “The Lady in the Lake”), Jessy Hodges (“Barry,” “Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed”), and Milan Carter (“It’s Florida Man,” “FUBAR”). 
	

	Exact character details are being kept under wraps. 


	Series creator Rachel Sennott leads the cast of “I Love LA,” with Odessa A’zion, True Whitaker, Jordan Firstman, and Josh Hutcherson also starring in Season 1. Season 2 is currently in production in Los Angeles. It will consist of eight episodes. 

	In the series, Sennott plays Maia, an aspiring talent manager who must juggle various relationships, including with her college bud turned rising star Tallulah (A’zion) and her schoolteacher boyfriend Dylan (Hutcherson).

	The show was renewed for a second season in November 2025 after just three episodes of the first season had aired. 

	As mentioned above, Sennott created the series and serves as executive producer. Emma Barrie, Aida Rodgers, Max Silvestri, and Lorene Scafaria also executive produce.  

	Egerton is repped by Range Media Partners, WME and Sloane Offer. Chung is repped by 3 Arts Entertainment, Gersh and Morris Yorn. Norris is repped by Paradigm and Strig Artist Management. Arnold is repped by Gersh and manager Kim Callahan. Hodges is repped by OPE Partners, Gersh Agency and Goodman Genow. Carter is repped by More Medavoy Management, Innovative Artists, and Ferrari Talent.
	

	(Pictured, from left to right: Taron Egerton, Jamie Chung, Dylan Arnold, Jessy Hodges, Milan Carter, Bejamin Norris)

schema.headline: ‘I Love LA’ Season 2: Taron Egerton, Jamie Chung Among 6 Cast in Guest Star Roles

title: ‘Gilmore Girls’ Documentary Set at HBO Max With Lauren Graham, Never-Before-Seen Footage and More
description:
It’s time to return to Star’s Hollow.

	An official documentary about “Gilmore Girls,” the beloved seven-season family dramedy that premiered in 200
body:
It’s time to return to Star’s Hollow.

	An official documentary about “Gilmore Girls,” the beloved seven-season family dramedy that premiered in 2000, is currently in production and set to debut on HBO Max. Per the official logline, the untitled film is told from the perspective of series creator Amy Sherman-Palladino alongside her husband, executive producer Daniel Palladino, and “reveals how the show eclipsed expectations to become a cross-generational phenomenon by unpacking the unique alchemy of the creators, cast, crew and collaborators. The film includes never-before-seen outtakes, behind-the-scenes footage and script pages.”
	

	Along with the Palladinos, the documentary will feature Lauren Graham, who starred in “Gilmore Girls” as Lorelai Gilmore, plus additional key cast and crew.


	Bonni Cohen serves as director on the documentary, which is produced by Sony Pictures Television’s This Machine, led by R.J. Cutler, in association with Warner Horizon Unscripted Television. Executive producers include Cutler, Jane Cha Cutler, the Palladinos, Mark Blatty, Elise Pearlstein and Trevor Smith. Cohen and Melissa Robledo serve as producers.

	“Gilmore Girls” was produced by Warner Bros. Television and aired on the WB for its first six seasons before moving to the CW for its seventh and final season from 2006 to 2007. Along with Graham, the cast included Alexis Bledel as Lorelai’s daughter, Rory Gilmore, as well as Melissa McCarthy, Keiko Agena, Yanic Truesdale, Scott Patterson, Kelly Bishop, Edward Herrmann, Liza Weil, Jared Padalecki, Milo Ventimiglia, Sean Gunn, Chris Eigeman and Matt Czuchry.
	

	While the Warner Bros. production is the first authorized documentary about “Gilmore Girls,” an unauthorized project called “Searching for Stars Hollow” was announced to be in the works in 2025 with Bishop, Padalecki, Chad Michael Murray and more set for interviews.

schema.headline: ‘Gilmore Girls’ Documentary Set at HBO Max With Lauren Graham, Never-Before-Seen Footage and More

title: Perez Hilton’s TikTok Account Banned After Disturbing Livestream and Hospitalization
description: Perez Hilton‘s TikTok account has been banned by the online platform after his disturbing livestream incident on Tuesday night where he appeared to
body:
Perez Hilton‘s TikTok account has been banned by the online platform after his disturbing livestream incident on Tuesday night where he appeared to harm himself.

	Police responded to a possible suicide attempt at Hilton’s Miami home, and he was hospitalized later Tuesday night. Viewers of Hilton’s TikTok livestream had contacted police after seeing him covered in blood and cutting himself with a knife. 


	A TikTok spokesperson told People that the platform’s automated moderation system flagged Hilton’s livestream after several minutes and that it was shut down after 15 minutes. The spokesperson added that a moderation error caused a delay in taking the livestream down.
	

	“Many of you have reached out with concern for Perez, and we are incredibly grateful for the overwhelming outpouring of love, support, and prayers,” Hilton’s family wrote in a statement on his blog. “We can confirm that Perez is receiving medical care, and our family’s focus right now is on his well-being. We kindly ask that you respect Perez’s privacy, as well as the privacy of his family, during this difficult time. If and when we are able to share any updates, we will do so with everyone as soon as we can. Thank you for your compassion, understanding, and continued support.”

	If you or anyone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please call the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline by dialing 988 or go to SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

schema.headline: Perez Hilton’s TikTok Account Banned After Disturbing Livestream and Hospitalization

title: Peyton List, Gustaf Skarsgård-Led Psychological Thriller ‘Exit to the Guillotine’ Wraps Filming (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Production has wrapped on “Exit to the Guillotine,” a psychological horror-thriller from Zachary Cotler starring Peyton List (“Cobra Kai,” “School S
body:
Production has wrapped on “Exit to the Guillotine,” a psychological horror-thriller from Zachary Cotler starring Peyton List (“Cobra Kai,” “School Spirits”) and Gustaf Skarsgård (“Oppenheimer,” “Vikings,” “Westworld”).

	The film follows Burne Peter (List), an off-Broadway actress who joins an international theater troupe at a decommissioned prison on the Ukrainian coast. The troupe, led by famous but unstable director Dado Levytskyy (Skarsgård), is rehearsing a new translation of an old Polish play. But each time they rehearse, an actor vanishes.
	

	The cast also features Ksenia Daniela Kharlamova (“Heated Rivalry”), Lea Myren (“The Ugly Stepsister”), Dylan Douglas (“Killing Hitler”), Marcin Czarnik (“Sunset,” “Son of Saul”), Nikki Si’ulepa (“The Whole of the Moon”), Michael Golab (“Splinter Cell: Deathwatch”), Pablo Sandstrom (“The Strangers,” “Day Drinker”) and introduces Jan Kłapyta.


	Cotler wrote and directed “Exit to the Guillotine.” Cotler’s films are produced under the Winter Film Company, an independent film company he founded.

	His directorial-debut drama “Maya Dardel,” about the titular writer who announces she intends to kill herself and that young male writers can compete to become the executor of her estate, won best screenplay at the Prague Independent Film Festival in 2017. His other credits include “When I’m a Moth,” a 2019 “un-biopic” of Hillary Rodham (pre-Clinton) set in 1969 Alaska, and “The Wall of Mexico,” a 2019 feature about a wealthy Mexican-American family who builds a wall around their ranch to stop townspeople from stealing their well water. 
	

	Producers include Magdalena Zyzak, Bonnie Timmermann, Marius Vilunas, Jean Pierre Magro and J. Todd Harris. List, Skarsgård, Thomas Pettinelli and Mark Jazwin are executive producers.

schema.headline: Peyton List, Gustaf Skarsgård-Led Psychological Thriller ‘Exit to the Guillotine’ Wraps Filming (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Why Higgsfield Inked Deals for AI Avatars of Streamer N3on, UFC’s Israel Adesanya and Quinton ‘Rampage’ Jackson, and More for New Film (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Higgsfield rankled some in the film industry in the spring with its showcase of its completely AI-generated “Hell Grind,” so almost in response, it’
body:
Higgsfield rankled some in the film industry in the spring with its showcase of its completely AI-generated “Hell Grind,” so almost in response, it’s brought some humans in the mix – in a sense.

	The AI startup’s next film, “Cully Hill Boys,” is still lacking in actual humans on the screen, but instead features characters modeled after the streamer N3on, UFC fighter Israel Adesanya, actor and UFC fighter Quinton “Rampage” Jackson and the basketball-focused influencer Matt Kiatipis. The 110-minute movie aims to be the first AI-generated production featuring legally licensed celebrity likenesses.
	

	Higgsfield’s movie — directed by “Hell Grind” director Aitore Zholdaskali and written by Tim Planagan from a script the company purchased from the screenplay submission service the Black List — is not meant to be a feature film marketed for public consumption, even if it’s telling a narrative and produced with humans involved. 


	Instead, the company intends for the project to showcase its Cinema Studio platform, one it hopes Hollywood studios adopt as they experiment with AI’s potential use cases. Even as Higgsfield promises the film isn’t meant for Hollywood’s content pool, the project is a test for how public figures can get paid to see their likenesses and scripts adapted with generative AI.

	But for Planagan, who has worked for years to get the story brought to life, seeing it produced in any fashion is a dream come true.

	“I’m just honored that the screenplay was selected as a story that kind of showcases their toolkit,” Planagan said in a video interview from his home in Portland, Oregon. “I haven’t seen the film yet, so I’m excited to see what their skilled group and talented folks were able to accomplish with that platform’s capabilities.”
	

	Planagan said his work on the project — set in East London, featuring a group of mobsters he said hadn’t been depicted in a film before — began years ago, with the feedback he received on iterations uploaded to the Black List helping shape the final product. But as producers approached him about developing his script, they wanted changes that would generalize the story — and pay him Writers Guild of America rates, though he’s not a guild member – but some he felt betrayed his script’s intent (such as, say, a desire to move the story from London to somewhere in the United States).

	“It’s a difficult thing to turn down,” he said. “When you have this scripture, you have to kind of really look within yourself and decide whether or not that’s something you’re willing to compromise on, and I just didn’t feel very comfortable doing it.”

	Then, roughly two months ago, came Higgsfield. In his conversations with the AI company, he was enamored by its respect for the screenplay and intrigued by the idea of seeing it brought to life using AI – even if the final product is just a showcase for the technology, tools Planagan doesn’t personally use for writing. 

	But despite the consternation in Hollywood about how AI models train off writers’ work, leading to the WGA to launch an #AINeedsHumans campaign as a rallying cry around the technology, Planagan said he wasn’t worried about such cases and that he’d let another story of his be adapted with the technology again. (Planagan’s agreement with Higgsfield, which he said was “on par” with WGA rates, was limited solely to AI adaptations.)

	“I would be honored to have another script displayed in this way,” said Planagan. “It’s more about being able to come up with a script that meets the quality requirements for storytelling at all. It’s very validating to to have your story used and read and wanted to be showcased for any purpose, so yeah, I would definitely do it.”

	Such is the same case for N3on, the digital moniker of 21-year-old Mikyle Rafiq. Rafiq, whose team brought him “Cully Hill Boys” as part of an array of potential opportunities, said he was “really, really excited” by the project — especially one that, according to him, only needed a two-minute voice recording and some photos to bring his likeness to life.
	

	“I’m streaming every day, so me trying to act in a movie and wake up at 6 a.m. and do all these things and come every day, it’s just unrealistic,” he said. “So this is a way to do it without having to do anything really.”

	Rafiq said the project, which gave him a “pretty good check with very little work,” aligned with his interest in the technology, one he says his legion of followers — he has 1.1 million YouTube subscribers and roughly 700,000 subscribers on the streaming platform Kick – already use to put him in “the weirdest situations” and make him do “the craziest things.” 

	Rafiq spoke to Variety after a Saturday incident during the Toronto Caribbean Festival where a golf cart he was on appeared to run over a woman as he was streaming. Rafiq was not driving the golf cart and emphasized that no one on his team was driving the cart, but he has since spoken to the victim, who he said went into surgery. “It was very, very, very unfortunate,” he said. 

	He plans to promote “Cully Hill Boys” on his streams, and should audiences respond well to the showcase, he could see himself in another AI-generated project.

	“I really want to continue doing stuff like this in the future,” he said. “I really want to see how everyone comes together and and sees and just to see what people think about it. But I think the feedback can be positive, and I want to keep continuing to do stuff like this.”

title: Avi Nash Joins FX Drama ‘Disinherited’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Avi Nash has joined the upcoming FX series “Disinherited” in a series regular role, Variety has learned exclusively. 

	Nash will appear alongside p
body:
Avi Nash has joined the upcoming FX series “Disinherited” in a series regular role, Variety has learned exclusively. 

	Nash will appear alongside previously announced leads Victoria Pedretti and Kiera Allen as well as fellow cast members Alan Ruck, Katja Herbers, Eddie Marsan and Jonathan Higginbotham. 

	The logline for the show states that Pedretti and Allen star as “a pair of scrappy sisters thrust by an unexpected inheritance into a world of generational wealth and long-buried crimes.” 
	

	Nash currently appears in the popular Apple TV series “Silo” in the role of Lukas. He has been with the show since it launched in 2023. He also recently starred in the drama feature “The Weight” opposite Ethan Hawke and Russell Crowe, which premiered at the Sundance Film Festival and will be released in theaters in September. He is known for his role as Siddiq in the hit AMC series “The Walking Dead” as well as “Silcon Valley,” and films like “There There” and “Learning to Drive.” 


	He is repped by Mosaic, The Way in the UK, and imPRint.

	“Disinherited” was originally announced with a pilot order at FX in June 2025, with the basic cabler ordering it to series in March 2026. Peter Gould is the writer and executive producer of “Disinherited,” while he also directed the pilot. Rian Johnson, Ram Bergman and Nena Rodrigue of T-Street executive produce along with Thomas Schnauz. FX Productions is the studio.

	Gould was previously the co-creator and showrunner on the hit AMC series “Better Call Saul.” He directed multiple episodes of that series as well, including the series finale. He was also a writer and producer on “Breaking Bad,” to which “Better Call Saul” was a prequel.

            The report notes Sidney was staying at an Embassy Suites in Georgia ... and an employee of the hotel called police to report another person had sexually assaulted a juvenile.
      

            Officers say they met with the kid and his parents at the hotel. The minor told cops that something had happened with Sidney, who is transgender.

Sidney claimed the guy approached her and told her she was "cute."

            As TMZ first reported ... Sidney was arrested Sunday for sodomy and child molestation. Cops said the boy was under 16. The officers said Sidney confessed to performing oral sex on the male.
      
    
            Records show the influencer remains behind bars on the charges.

title: Kristi Noem and Corey Lewandowski Spotted Spending Time Together in Minnesota
description:
KRISTI NOEM & COREY LEWANDOWSKI
                          PEDALING ROMANCE RUMORS?!?
body:
KRISTI NOEM & COREY LEWANDOWSKI
                          PEDALING ROMANCE RUMORS?!?
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 5, 2026
                            12:23 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 5, 2026
                                1:53 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Kristi Noem and Corey Lewandowski appear a lot closer than they might want people to believe ... because the two were seen spending some quality time together in Minnesota.
      
    
            In new footage -- obtained by TMZ -- the duo is seen biking along the shores of Lake Minnetonka Tuesday afternoon before settling in at an outdoor table at The Grocer's Table, a cozy market and café in Wayzata.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Corey's keeping it casual in a tight T-shirt and a fresh pair of shades, while Kristi tried to keep a low profile in a flannel shirt and floppy hat.
      

            Kristi and Corey later pedaled over to CōV, a local restaurant ... where they were clearly enjoying each other's company -- laughing and leaning toward one another.
      
    
            Corey appears to notice a bystander filming them ... and quickly turns his head away from the camera.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            An eyewitness tells us the pair was all smiles and kept close throughout the outing.
      
    
            Rumors have swirled for years that Noem and Lewandowski are romantically involved -- claims both of them have denied.
      
    
            In March, Noem was pressed in a House Judiciary Committee hearing about whether she had sexual relations with Lewandowski while serving as the head of the Department of Homeland Security ... a question she dismissed as "tabloid garbage."
      
    
            Lewandowski served as an unpaid adviser to Noem at DHS and is no longer with the department.  
      
    
            We reached out to Noem and Lewandowski for comment ... so far, no word back.

'RHOBH' Star Amanda Frances

                              August 5, 2026
                            1:01 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Amanda Frances won't be holding a diamond for another season of "The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills" ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Sources close to the show tell TMZ ... producers did not ask the season 15 newbie to return for season 16.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Amanda's departure comes after a rocky rookie season ... she clashed with Dorit Kemsley and Bozoma Saint John claimed she was building a "cult" through her business.
      

            The decision may come as a surprise to Amanda, who recently said she believed there was a "good chance" Bravo would invite her back ... though she admitted she wasn't certain she would accept the offer.
      
    
            Amanda told "Extra" filming and promoting the show essentially consumed an entire year of her life, adding the experience took up a significant amount of "psychological space" while she continued running her business.
      
    
            Despite the challenges, Amanda said she was grateful for the opportunities and relationships the show brought her.
      
    
            Farewell!!!
